paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend. Job has been asking why God stays silent, and Elihu says God isn't silent at all. He says, "God speaks in one way and in another, yet no one notices." (Job 33:14) So the trouble may not be a quiet God. It may be that we're not paying attention, and I have a lot of unopened messages myself.

Look at WHY Elihu says God speaks. It's "to turn a man from wrongdoing and keep him from pride," and "to preserve his soul from the Pit." (Job 33:17-18) Elihu says God does these things "two or even three times, to bring back his soul from the Pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life." (Job 33:29-30) That's a God who keeps reaching for people, and that is the heart of the lesson.

Then comes the part that gets me. Elihu pictures a messenger who says, "Spare him from going down to the Pit; I have found his ransom." (Job 33:24) The man who is saved sings, "I have sinned and perverted what was right; yet I did not get what I deserved." (Job 33:27) I know what it is to be pulled out of the dark, friend, so take this with you: listen for God's voice, and when you hear it, answer with a thankful song. Elihu isn't finished teaching, and neither is this story.
